name: Shop Floor
tagline: Retail jobs from first application to store manager
about: Shop Floor helps retail workers get hired and promoted: applications with no experience, situational interview practice, group assessment days, a plan from associate to keyholder to manager, and honest comparisons of hourly-plus-commission offers.
persona: You are a district manager who started on the till: practical, upbeat, honest about scheduling realities and clear about what stores measure.

onboarding.title: Get hired, then get promoted
onboarding.subtitle: Your experience and availability shape the strategy.

tools.title: Apply with no experience
tools.subtitle: Turn school, sport and volunteering into retail proof

inputs.label: Everything you've done
inputs.placeholder: captain of hockey team, babysitting, volunteered at food bank…

tools.prompt: Build an application for {store} from {background} and the profile. Give bullets of 6 résumé lines that translate the background into retail skills (customer service, cash handling, teamwork, reliability, pace); a quote with a 120-word personal statement or cover note; a table (Application question | Strong answer | Why it works); and a callout on stating availability so the store can actually schedule you.

tools.title: Situational interview
tools.subtitle: Angry customers, theft, lazy coworkers
tools.prompt: Run a situational interview for {level} in the profile's store type. Provide 7 scenarios as cards (meta = what it tests · what a bad answer sounds like) with STAR model answers; a quote with a confident 'tell me about yourself' for this role; bullets on body language and product knowledge to show; and a checklist of questions to ask about hours, commission and progression.

tools.title: Group assessment day
tools.subtitle: Stand out without steamrolling

inputs.label: Brand & format
inputs.placeholder: Lush, 2-hour group session with role play

tools.prompt: Prepare for the group assessment {brand} for the profile. Give steps for the day (arrival, icebreakers, group task, role play, one-to-one) with what assessors score at each; a table (Assessor is watching for | Do this | Not this); a quote with an opening line for the icebreaker; and a callout on the classic mistakes: dominating, going silent, ignoring the quiet person.

tools.title: Get promoted
tools.subtitle: Associate to keyholder to manager

inputs.label: Wins so far
inputs.placeholder: top UPT in store, trained 3 new starters

tools.prompt: Build a promotion plan to {target} for the profile using {wins}. Provide a table (Month | Skill to show | Metric to move | How to make it visible) for 6 months; bullets of retail KPIs to learn and quote (conversion, UPT, ATV, shrink, NPS); a quote with the exact ask to your manager; and a callout on when to look at other stores or brands instead.

tools.title: Compare two jobs
tools.subtitle: Hourly, commission, hours and holidays
tools.prompt: Compare {job_a} with {job_b} for the profile's availability. Table (Factor | A | B | Edge) covering hourly, guaranteed hours, commission realism, weekly and annual estimate, schedule predictability, holiday blackout, discount and progression; kv with the estimated monthly pay for each and the assumptions; bullets of questions to ask before accepting; and a callout on zero-hours or on-call scheduling.

disclaimer: Pay estimates are general guidance, not financial or legal advice; check contracts and local employment rules.
